subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: Should OpenClaw accept the current-head MXC native dependency graph and upstream `--config-base64` argv transport for this first-party external sandbox plugin?
rationale: The remaining blocker is not a mechanical code defect: it is whether maintainers and secops accept the native Microsoft MXC binaries, `node-pty` install-script dependency, lock/shrinkwrap changes, and same-user argv exposure boundary for sandbox configs.

options.title: Approve exact dependency boundary
options.body: A maintainer/secops owner reviews and approves the current head dependency graph and accepts the MXC SDK preview transport as an opt-in plugin boundary.

options.title: Pause for safer SDK transport
options.body: Keep the PR open or paused until upstream MXC provides a non-argv config transport that avoids exposing encoded sandbox config in process arguments.

options.title: Close as not worth core-owned official support
options.body: Reject the first-party plugin path and ask for MXC support to remain outside OpenClaw until the dependency and sandbox boundary are lower-risk.

recommendation.title: Approve exact dependency boundary
recommendation.body: A maintainer/secops owner reviews and approves the current head dependency graph and accepts the MXC SDK preview transport as an opt-in plugin boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR is assigned to `steipete`, and his prior sandbox backend work makes him the best available owner to coordinate the maintainer/security boundary decision.
